items.title: US egg producer to cull 1.8mil birds after bird flu outbreak
items.summary: Cal-Maine Foods said on Wednesday it would cull about 1.8 million birds after avian influenza was detected at one of its Florida facilities, forcing the US egg producer to temporarily halt production at the site. The company said it has suspended production at the facility while following US Department of Agriculture protocols, and will cull 1.4 million laying hens and 360,000 pullets, representing 2.7 per cent of its flock. According to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), "the human health risk to the general US public from HPAI viruses is considered low."

items.title: MCMC clarifies Nov 19 disaster alert system test
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has clarified that the test of the National Disaster Warning System scheduled for today is an internal technical exercise and will not involve public alerts. In a statement, the commission said the exercise was intended to assess the system's technical readiness and was not a public warning test in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Kelantan and Pahang. However, the system requires a functioning mobile network and compatible devices to receive the alerts.

items.title: Malaysia, US to strengthen cooperation on sovereign AI cloud
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and the United States intend to strengthen cooperation in developing Malaysia's Sovereign Artificial Intelligence (AI) Cloud, with Washington indicating potential support of US$50 million for the initiative. The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) in a statement said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and US President Donald Trump today announced their intention to pursue cooperation in support of the Malaysia-led initiative, including through the participation of US technology companies. Under the initiative, Malaysia will determine the design, procurement and operational arrangements for the Sovereign AI Cloud.

items.title: No to renaming breakfast marmalade! UK govt slams 'myths' over EU talks
items.summary: LONDON: No, the UK won't have to ban smoky bacon crisps, and no, British breakfast favourite marmalade won't need to be renamed. The UK government says the food and drinks deal alone could add £5.1 billion (US$6.7 billion) to the country's economy. "Smoky flavours in crisps, sauces, and soups will remain on UK supermarket shelves," the government statement said.

items.title: IAEA says North Korea is expanding uranium-enrichment plant at Yongbyon
items.summary: VIENNA: North Korea has built an extension to its original uranium-enrichment plant at its Yongbyon nuclear complex as it continues to expand its production of weapons-grade material, UN nuclear watchdog chief Rafael Grossi said on Wednesday. The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has not had access to North Korea since Pyongyang expelled its inspectors in 2009. North Korea, formally known as the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), has carried out several nuclear tests and appears to continue to produce the two materials with which one can make the core of a nuclear weapon - highly enriched uranium and plutonium.

items.title: OPEC speaks up for fossil fuels at COP31 climate talks
items.summary: ANTALYA: Efforts to boost electrification will depend on fossil fuels, OPEC Secretary General Haitham Al Ghais said on Wednesday at the COP31 talks, where host Turkiye is seeking to make increased electricity use a central outcome of the conference. Al Ghais also said electrification was not a panacea. Turkiye's own energy system relies on fossil fuels.

items.title: Man, 16-year-old son charged with murder of youth in Sibu
items.summary: SIBU: A man and his 16-year-old son were jointly charged at the magistrate's court with murdering a 19-year-old youth in a fight at Taman Foochow, Jalan Gambir, earlier this month. They were accused of murdering Ryuichi Hii Shan Jie about 12.30am on Nov 7 and charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or jail of between 30 and 40 years. Deputy public prosecutor Mohd Syazani Izzaddin Abdul Muadzam appeared for the prosecution, while the accused were represented by lawyer Boston Ho.

items.title: Israeli spy chief lobbied for joint Iran strikes on US visit
items.summary: TEL AVIV: The head of Israel's Mossad spy agency, Roman Gofman, advocated for joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran during meetings with US officials last week, according to two people briefed on the visit. Gofman met with Trump administration officials, including CIA Director John Ratcliffe, in Washington, the people said, adding that the Mossad chief briefed the officials on Israeli intelligence on Iran. In his meetings, Gofman briefed US officials on Israeli intelligence on Iran, the two people said.

items.title: Heart-stopping sight: 2 children seen playing outside high-rise windows
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA: Two children, aged 6 and 7, were spotted playing on a narrow ledge outside a high-rise apartment building here after they were believed to have been left home alone without parental supervision. The incident, which occurred at 4.26pm on Nov 13, came to light after videos showing the children walking barefoot along the building's exterior went viral on social media. Subang Jaya deputy police chief Superintendent Mohd Fairus Jaafar said preliminary investigations found that the children had apparently climbed out through a window before playing on the building's exterior structure.

items.title: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for next US House speaker
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Democrats elected this month to the US House of Representatives nominated Hakeem Jeffries on Wednesday to lead them in the next Congress, putting him on the precipice of becoming the nation's first Black House speaker. The incoming House Democratic Caucus nominated Jeffries in a closed-door, secret-ballot vote. The speaker election requires 218 votes on the House floor.

items.title: Thailand, Cambodia to hold third maritime talks in KL on Nov 24 to 27
items.summary: Thailand's Foreign Ministry said the meeting, organised by the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA), would build on discussions held during the second meeting in The Hague, the Netherlands, particularly regarding the technical aspects of maritime delimitation. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow, who is also Thailand's Agent, will lead the Thai delegation, accompanied by Deputy Prime Minister Pakorn Nilprapunt, who will serve as an adviser, the ministry said in a statement on Wednesday. The second meeting in The Hague last October focused on the presentation of viewpoints and technical information concerning maritime delimitation, with Thailand providing relevant technical details to the commission.

items.title: Britain's Prince William visits Bollywood studio, watches dancers
items.summary: MUMBAI: Britain's Prince William watched Bollywood dances and toured a film studio in Mumbai on the last day of his royal visit to India on Wednesday, while his wife, Kate Middleton, spoke to health workers at a maternity hospital in the city. William and Kate had separate engagements on Wednesday, with the prince visiting the office of a prominent Bollywood production house, Dharma Productions, in suburban Mumbai, while Kate visited a maternity hospital in the centre of the city. William smiled and clapped as dancers moved to a number from Dharma's hit Bollywood movie, "Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham" (Joy Sometimes, Sorrow Sometimes), which is set partly in London.

items.title: Endoscopy equipment spared in Kuantan hospital lorry fire
items.summary: KUANTAN: A three-tonne lorry carrying endoscopy machines and equipment was partially destroyed in a fire at Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital today. The Pahang Health Department said the equipment was not affected by the fire, which broke out at 4.15pm. "The hospital's Emergency Response Team took initial action before the Fire and Rescue Department arrived and fully extinguished the blaze.

items.title: Kuala Kangsar Form Three death: Anwar orders immediate probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the authorities to conduct an immediate, thorough and transparent investigation into the death of a Form Three student at a school in Perak today. He also conveyed his condolences to the student's family. Al-Fatihah," he said.

items.title: Court reserves decision on Tan Kok Ping's appeal on defamation award to Penang CM
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today reserved its decision on businessman Tan Sri Tan Kok Ping's appeal against a High Court ruling ordering him to pay RM350,000 in damages to Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow for defamation. A three-member panel comprising Justices Datuk Azizul Azmi Adnan, Datuk Aliza Sulaiman and Datuk Seri Latifah Mohd Tahar reserved its decision after hearing submissions from Tan's counsel, Datuk K. Kirubakaran, and Chow's counsel, K. Simon Murali. On Dec 3, 2024, the Penang High Court ordered Tan to pay RM350,000 in damages after finding that remarks he made at a press conference on Oct 18, 2023, were defamatory.

items.title: Home is a dim hope for West Bank's displaced Palestinians
items.summary: AFTER Israeli forces pushed him and thousands of others out of the West Bank refugee camp of Tulkarem last year, Adel Darsieh held onto his hope of returning home, but it is fading fast. said the 64-year-old. said Darsieh.

items.title: The real business of diplomacy at Asean Summit in Manila
items.summary: THE first morning of the 49th Asean Summit in Manila brought a welcome gesture from Indonesia President Prabowo Subianto. Some expectations of Asean are unreasonable. Leaders also called for ratification of the agreement establishing an Asean coordinating centre for haze control.

items.title: NST Leader: Malaysia must draw tourists beyond KL, Penang and Johor Baru
items.summary: Of course, London, New York and Paris are the premier urban tourism powerhouses offering cultural depth and global connectivity while competing on iconic recognition and experiential depth rather than value. What about Malaysia? Besides boosting Kuala Lumpur's appeal as a night-time tourism destination, the I Lite U 2.0 urban lighting project supports Malaysia's target of 47 million international arrivals and RM329 billion in tourism receipts for Visit Malaysia 2026.

items.title: Don't panic if your phone alarm goes off tomorrow, it's only a drill
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The national Cell Broadcast System (CBS), designed to deliver disaster warnings directly to mobile phones, will undergo live testing tomorrow. Developed by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), the system will send alerts to mobile phones in affected areas without requiring recipients' phone numbers, SMS services or an internet connection. The system broadcasts alerts through mobile networks to compatible devices within designated areas.

items.title: AI growth must be backed by safeguards, support structures
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The government is committed to strengthening policies, support structures and high-speed digital infrastructure to protect Malaysians while ensuring the country fully harnesses the economic benefits of artificial intelligence (AI), said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said the government was taking a deliberate and purposeful approach to governance to ensure adequate safeguards for citizens as AI transforms industries and reshapes the employment landscape. "Because of AI and how AI changes the way some businesses, some industries, some sectors work," he said during a panel session titled "The AI Wave, Malaysia's Next Move" at the Putrajaya Festival of Ideas (FOI) 2026.

items.title: Wan Rosdy calls for probe into Pua's disclosure of Pardons Board minutes
items.summary: KUANTAN: The disclosure of purported Pardons Board meeting minutes concerning Datuk Seri Najib Abdul Razak's house arrest order by former DAP lawmaker Tony Pua has raised concerns over the confidentiality and security of government records. Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the disclosure raised questions about the handling and governance of official documents. "How could documents relating to the official proceedings of the Pardons Board be made public?

items.title: Sri Maha Mariamman Temple clarifies Anwar, Macron did not enter inner sanctum with shoes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The management of Sri Maha Mariamman Temple here has dismissed claims of religious disrespect following an unscheduled visit by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and French President Emmanuel Macron yesterday, clarifying that the leaders did not enter the temple's inner sanctum. Temple chairman Tan Sri Dr R. Nadarajah said the brief stopover was unplanned, with the management receiving no prior notification from the authorities or organisers. "Nobody can enter the inner sanctum wearing shoes.

items.title: Zahid prays for recovery of policemen injured in Tapah crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has prayed for the recovery of policemen injured in an accident in Tapah, Perak, yesterday. Zahid said he had been briefed on the condition of those currently receiving treatment at Slim River Hospital, including Lance Corporal Ridzuan Sarizan from the Bagan Datuk district police headquarters. Zahid, who is also Bagan Datuk member of parliament, said his political secretary, Datuk Abdul Aziz Julkarnain, visited several of the personnel undergoing treatment at Slim River Hospital today on his behalf.

items.title: Flash floods hit Puncak Alam, Meru for second consecutive night
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Flash floods struck parts of Puncak Alam for the second consecutive day today, with several roads inundated following heavy rain this evening. A Threads user, @frhanirhmn, shared footage of the flooding at 8.16pm, showing muddy floodwaters covering sections of the road. The flooding affected Jalan Bukit Cherakah heading towards Meru, where another video showed vehicles navigating a waterlogged stretch.

items.title: Sultan Sharafuddin impressed by Merdeka Textile Museum
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, has expressed admiration for the establishment of the Merdeka Textile Museum and its role in preserving and showcasing the rich textile heritage of the Malay world. In a Selangor Royal Office Facebook post, Sultan Sharafuddin said he was particularly impressed by the museum's curatorial standards and the meticulous arrangement and presentation of its collection of fabrics, traditional attire and textiles. "I am greatly impressed by the establishment of the Merdeka Textile Museum and its role in highlighting the history, artistry and craftsmanship of traditional Malay textiles.

items.title: Student death probe: Kuala Kangsar boarding school instructed to give full cooperation
items.summary: IPOH: The Perak Education Department has instructed a school in Kuala Kangsar to cooperate fully with police following the death of a Form Three student on its grounds today. "The department has instructed the school to give its full cooperation to the police," it said. The department also expressed its condolences to the student's family.

items.title: RON97, RON95 and diesel prices drop by up to 20 sen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The retail price of unsubsidised RON97 will drop by 20 sen per litre, while unsubsidised RON95 and diesel prices will each fall by 15 sen for the Nov 19 to 25 period. The Finance Ministry (MOF) said in a statement that the new price of unsubsidised RON97 would be RM4 per litre, while RON95 would be RM3.72 and diesel RM4.72 per litre. "Supplies of petroleum products continue to increase despite several constraints that could affect market price stability.

items.title: Lynas permanent disposal facility 79pct complete
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Construction of Lynas' permanent disposal facility (PDF) has reached 79 per cent as of Oct 31, the Dewan Rakyat was told. Deputy Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Dr Mohammad Yusof Apdal said 1.46 million metric tonnes of WLP (water leach purification) residue has been transferred into it. "The Atomic Energy Licensing Board (AELB) is regularly monitoring construction and Lynas' compliance with its licence conditions.

items.summary: MISSED what happened today? items.title: Semporna losing its edge as accommodation, dive costs climb
items.summary: SEMPORNA: Rising accommodation and diving package costs are making Semporna less competitive compared with international dive destinations, says a diver from Peninsular Malaysia. "As a diver from Peninsular Malaysia, I think prices in Semporna have gone out of hand. He said resorts offering Sipadan diving packages generally required a minimum booking of three to four nights, but guests would get only one day of diving at the world-renowned island.
